statement: You receive two separately sorted chains. Merge them into one ascending chain by splicing nodes - repeatedly take the smaller of the two current heads - and print the merged chain on one line, separated by single spaces. When one chain runs out, the remainder of the other is appended as a whole.
constraints: Each input chain is sorted ascending; an empty chain is an empty line.

example.why: Equal heads may be taken from either side; every step takes a current minimum.

hint: A dummy head and a tail pointer turn the whole merge into one calm loop plus one final splice.
mistake: Dropping the leftover tail after one chain empties - the loop ends, but the merge is only done after the splice.
